_README: Author "def": what the thing IS, in one learner-facing clause — not a list
of other translations, which the `en` gloss already gives. Match the sense
in `en`; never drift to another homograph.
"expect" is what the corpus holds now; fix-authored.ts refuses a stale row.

expect.def: motion, movement, progress, way, going; in gear, progressing, working, going
life; being alive; life; way of life (a particular manner of behaving and passing one’s time, whether real or ideal, and whether self-chosen or not)
to change, to alter; to change, to vary
difficult, hard, challenging, tough; difficult, prickly
to decide, to make a decision; to opt, to decide
to establish; to enforce; to cause to become prevalent, accepted, or effective; to establish oneself; to become prevalent, accepted, or effective
entire, whole, complete; whole, intact
so, such, that; so, thus, like this/that, in this/that way, in this/that manner

rows.en: direct, straight, without deviation or interruption

expect.def: direct, straight, without deviation or interruption; direct, candid, forthright (of a person, conversation)
absolutely, fully, entirely; absolutely, definitely, certainly, in any case
clear; transparent; bright; clear; unambiguous; understood
now, at this moment; now, then; expressing a logical or temporal consequence
roll, reel, spool; roll, tube

rows.en: just, simply, indicating that something is generally known or cannot be changed, and is therefore to be accepted

expect.def: just, simply, indicating that something is generally known or cannot be changed, and is therefore to be accepted; often equivalent to a shrug; just, quickly, indicating that something is done fast or without much complication
to receive (something given, sent, won, etc.); to receive (a rebuke, punishment, fine, prison sentence, etc.)
at all; even; even; expressing a climax
within, inside (spatial); within, in the space of (temporal)

expect.def: to create, to call into being; to create, make, form, shape
article; article, item, ware

outside, beyond; outside

cable, line, wire; line
alcohol, ethanol (substance); alcohol, liquor (beverage containing the former substance)
manager (see usage notes below) (male or of unspecified sex, sometimes female); agent of an artist or sportsperson (male or of unspecified sex, sometimes female)
